column2:
Are there any processes in place to monitor the level of reuse of your country's open data?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) briefly describe these processes and (2) provide the URLs to support the answer.
column4: Open Data Portal  has tools in place to monitor data usage. Google Analytics is used to monitor data user behaviour as well. Also, a study was carried out in June 2022 to determine the level of the re-use of open data, the impact of open data etc. among public sector institutions (https://data.gov.lt/news/27). An overview of this study was published in September 2022 - https://data.gov.lt/news/30
column7:
1. The National Open Data Portal has tools to monitor data usage, including views, searches, downloads, feedback/comments on data quality.
2. Google Analytics is also used to track user behavior.
3. In June 2022, a study was conducted to evaluate the reuse of open data and its impact among public sector institutions. An overview of this study was published in September 2022. You can find more details here: (https://data.gov.lt/blog/2022/06/20/atlikta-duomenu-atverimo-pazangos-ir-poveikio-vertinimo-apklausa/) and the overview here: (https://data.gov.lt/blog/2022/09/29/kvieciame-susipazinti-su-pirminiais-atviru-duomenu-pazangos-ir-poveikio-vertinimo-apklausos-rezultatais/).
4. The open data license (CC BY) requires users to cite the data source, which helps us identify such cases using search engines (Google etc.).
5. The State Data Agency regularly showcases the best examples of open data usage at public events, seminars, workshops, and conferences. This task requires a regular scanning of media, social media, and scientific chat groups to find the most recent examples.

column4:
A study/questionaire for institutions was carried out in June 2022 to determine the level of the re-use of open data, the impact of open data etc. among public sector institutions (https://data.gov.lt/news/27). An overview of this study was published in September 2022 - https://data.gov.lt/news/30. 
The Ministry of Economy and Innovations periodically promotes re-use of open data seeking to show a sense of data opening for institutions:
https://eimin.lrv.lt/lt/naujienos/auga-tiek-atvertu-duomenu-kiekis-tiek-domejimasis-jais

column7:
Most efforts are focused on persuading institutions to open their data, but several incentives are in place to encourage the reuse monitoring process:
1. The State Data Agency leads an RRF-funded project aimed at centralizing national data and producing open data. This provides a strong incentive to monitor and collect best practices for using open data to convince other institutions to share their data with the centralized Data Lake.
2. The State Data Agency makes public announcements each time it opens a dataset (https://duomenys.stat.gov.lt/naujienos/). After these announcements, the Agency searches for examples and use cases of reused published data. There is a feedback loop for agencies that provided the data for opening to receive feedback about data quality. Additionally, there is a centralized place to collect open data requests and an automated process to respond to such requests.
3. As mentioned in the previous response (question I2, answer 3), a survey conducted in June 2022 evaluates the reuse of open data and its impact among public sector institutions.
4. The Ministry of Economy and Innovation periodically promotes the reuse of open data to showcase the value of data openness for institutions:
https://eimin.lrv.lt/lt/ziniasklaidai/naujienos/eimin-didesnis-duomenu-prieinamumas-ir-pakartotinis-naudojimas-leistu-sutaupyti-daugiau-kaip-4-mln-euru-valstybes-lesu/

https://eimin.lrv.lt/lt/ziniasklaidai/naujienos/eimin-iniciatyva-atveriama-dar-daugiau-svarbiu-duomenu/

For Explanation:

column4: "Transparency International Lithuania” collaborating with the Parliament to obtain data created online political integrity monitoring tool called Manoseimas.lt. The tool contains agendas of Members of Parliament including their meetings with interest groups and registered lobbyists allowing to compare the activity of individual MPs as well as different political groups. Moreover, recently the tool was updated with the data about long-term permits to access the Parliament, being one of the very few countries in the world to publish such information. Permits data was also matched with data from parliamentary committees meetings to see who and how much used their permits to participate in commitees discussions. Currently, Manoseimas.lt is being updated with 4 years data on committees’ meetings.
column7:
1. As mentioned in question I3, answer 2, the National Open Data Portal includes a feature for the civil society to request new open data. This functionality is promoted at every conference, workshop, and presentation in which the State Data Agency participates.
2. The State Data Agency frequently meets with higher education institutions (both students and teachers) to discuss available open datasets and explore potential research topics. We are aware of at least three master's level students using our open data in their theses.
3. The State Data Agency offers virtual environments with sensitive anonymized data for safe analysis. Some requests for sensitive data access are redirected to a different track, resulting in the creation of demand-driven open data collections accessible to everyone instead of private access.
4. The State Data Agency, as the national statistics bureau, frequently receives inquiries about statistical indicators. Recently, the agency has developed a practice of converting individual single-indicator requests into universal demand-driven open datasets, allowing for wider reuse and more nuanced analysis, as this data is more detailed than simple statistical indicators.
5. As the State Data Agency leads an RRF-funded project aimed at centralizing national data into a single Data Lake, one of its tasks is to systematically interview every potential data provider. So far, approximately 300 in-depth interviews have been conducted. Data providers are incentivized to share their data with the promise that making some data open will significantly reduce the burden of individual requests from the public, such as custom statistical indicators. Institutions are asked about the most frequent public requests, and these responses are treated as an indirect public survey ("what do people want to know"), leading to the publication of more useful datasets.
6. "Transparency International Lithuania," in collaboration with the Parliament, created an online political integrity monitoring tool called Manoseimas.lt. This tool includes the agendas of Members of Parliament, their meetings with interest groups, and registered lobbyists, allowing for comparisons between individual MPs and different political groups. Recently, the tool was updated with data on long-term permits to access the Parliament, making Lithuania one of the few countries to publish such information. Permit data was also matched with parliamentary committee meetings to track permit usage for committee discussions.
7. The national Open Data conference, "Open Data Opportunities - See What is Not Visible!" aimed to present the work done by the public sector and the current affairs of data users. During the event, representatives from the OECD, Lithuania's public sector, business, and the academic community shared their current challenges, opportunities, and experiences in data impact and reuse (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=owjZYMphpBI).
8. The Information Society Committee cooperates with Mykolas Romeris University, presenting to master's students about the possibilities of open data.

column2: 4.3 Created impact
4.3a Governmental impact

Is any data on the impact created by open data on governmental challenges (e.g. efficiency, effectiveness, transparency, decision-making capacity) available in your country such as from research studies, impact assessments, or other systematic investigations that quantify the results or broader effects of open data being reused?

For Explanation:
* If yes, please (1) specify what kind of data source proves this impact and (2) provide the URLs to this data.
column4:
To advance data opening and digital transformation across different fields of public administration, the Government has established an Open Data and Digital Transformation Centre of Excellence, which is responsible for assisting institutions in their activities regarding planning of data opening and digital transformation and project implementation, coordination of inter-institutional activities, initiating of shared solutions and ensuring quality of implementation, dissemination of knowledge needed to open data and implement digital transformation, and monitoring of the implementation of initiatives. (https://lrv.lt/en/news/green-light-to-initiative-to-proceed-with-open-data-and-digital-transformation-centre-of-excellence)

In the middle of 2022 Open Data Progress and Impact Assessment survey was conducted by Ministry of Economy and Innovation and Information Society Development Committee. 165 state and municipal institutions and bodies participated in it. The results showed that the majority of respondents positively assess the impact of open data on the economy, social and political environment. Institutional respondents used open data in implementing regulatory policies. (https://data.gov.lt/news/30)

Datasets regarding different topics can be found on our national data portal, here are some examples classified by topics: Government and Public sector datasets - https://data.gov.lt/datasets?category_id=231 ; Justice, legal system and public safety datasets - https://data.gov.lt/datasets?category_id=139

State Enterprise Centre of Registers is one of the main state data managers, which has its Open data strategy (https://www.registrucentras.lt/bylos/dokumentai/duomenys/aduomenys/Duomenu_atverimo_strategija_2020-06-26_Final_papildyta_2020-08-17.pdf).

The Government of the Republic of Lithuania uses national and international resources of open data in solving the deep problems, decision making, preparation of strategic management documents, such as annual activity reports (https://lrv.lt/lt/aktuali-informacija/xvii-vyriausybe/strateginis-valdymas/vyriausybes-veiklos-ataskaitos-seimui).

column7:
Road traffic information system of state importance, called EIS. The purpose of creating this system is to enable road users and road maintenance companies to use traffic data collected automatically and stored in one place. Data is collected into the EIS from several automatic weather stations, called KOS stations. These are roadside devices with sensors that measure parameters needed to determine road condition and traffic conditions (road surface temperature, air temperature and relative humidity, dew point, wind direction, speed and gusts, intensity and type of precipitation, visibility, road surface condition, frozen depth of road structures, etc.). The system also collects video data, which is collected from cameras installed and additionally installed at KOS stations. Another and no less important goal of EIS is to inform road users about traffic conditions, traffic disturbances, applied traffic management measures on roads and to provide users with the opportunity to perform automated traffic data analysis. 
URL to reuse case: https://eismoinfo.lt/#!/

1. The State Data Agency employs and promotes a hiring practice in which candidates are given an openly accessible dataset to analyze, allowing them to demonstrate their competence and showcase their creativity.
2. The State Data Agency organizes school competitions that require participants to use open data.
3. Various educational institutions, such as Turing College, LSMU, and CodeAcademy, organize hackathons that utilize national open data.
4. Students are enthusiastic about shifting from synthetic or small real datasets to using real-world data, where the number of rows often reaches tens of millions.

The three-dimensional map of the real situation allows not only to see the city virtually, but also to assess the changes taking place in it. The 3D city map allows the municipality and design, real estate companies and all those contributing to the city's well-being to understand what impact the planned projects will have on the city's development and the well-being of the citizens.  - 3D model of a real image - the current situation of the city is presented, it provides an opportunity to get acquainted with the changes and directions of development of the city.

 - Oblique view aerial photos - the territory and the objects in it are depicted from different sides. You can see the park near your house from different angles.
